sources.entry: flatnotes - Database-less note-taking web app that utilises a flat folder of markdown files for storage. (Demo) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted, database-less note-taking web app that stores notes as a flat folder of markdown files.
summary.what_it_does: flatnotes is a web app for taking notes, with each note saved as a plain markdown file in a single folder rather than in a database. It offers raw and WYSIWYG markdown editing, full-text and advanced search (with "/" as a shortcut from anywhere in the app), and note tagging. Notes can link to each other with wikilink syntax such as [[My Other Note]]. The README says the search index is the only thing cached and is incrementally synced on each search and at startup, so files can be added, edited or deleted outside the app while it runs. It also lists a customisable home page, light and dark themes, a mobile-responsive interface, and a RESTful API. Authentication options are none, read-only, username/password, and 2FA.
use_cases: markdown notes in a plain folder
how_to_run: Or use the Docker Compose example in the README (image dullage/flatnotes:latest, volume ./data:/data, port 8080:8080)
See the Environment Variables article in the wiki for the full list of configuration options
notable: Notes are plain markdown files in a flat folder with no database, so they can be moved to another app at any time
Search index is incrementally synced, so external edits to the folder are picked up
Multiple authentication modes including 2FA and read-only
caveats: The README says the demo site resets every 15 minutes
The roadmap deliberately limits new features to keep the app simple
Self-hosting is recommended via Docker; no other install method is described in the README
